title: The change that charged two plans in one day
blurb: Proration double-billed the switch day and retries re-charged.
prompt: A plan change on the 31st billed both plans for that day, and a processor timeout retry created a second charge under a fresh idempotency key. The billing run also charged before recording its marker. Review it, fix it, and prove proration is exclusive and charging is idempotent.
aiNote: The draft prorates with a fixed 30-day divisor and charges both plans on the switch day, and its billing run charges before claiming its idempotency marker and retries timeouts under fresh keys, so retries can double-charge.
testIdea: Change plans mid-month and assert the two line amounts sum to exactly one month; crash between charge and marker and assert the retry run does not charge again; time out a charge and assert reconciliation precedes any retry.
followUps: What proration policy is fairest and why?
How do credits flow into a later invoice?
What state must survive a processor outage mid-run?
